Alger, 27 novembre 2026 (Algeria Tech) —: Algiers, November 27, 2026 (Algeria Tech) — The city of Oran has climbed to the nineteenth global spot in Ookla's Speedtest Global Index, marking a notable progression of eleven places compared to the previous month. The performance of national telecommunications infrastructures shows noticeable increases, driven by the expansion of digital access and mobile speeds.
Une progression remarquable des performa: A remarkable progression in mobile performance in Oran and Algiers
La capitale de l'Ouest algérien intègre: The capital of western Algeria joins the closed circle of the twenty fastest cities on the planet for mobile connection, according to the latest monthly update by the American company Ookla. This advance propels Oran to the nineteenth global rank, illustrating a gain of eleven positions compared to the thirtieth rank previously occupied. Data released by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications specify that less than three months ago, the city was still in the forty-first global position with a download speed of 197.09 megabits per second. The observed acceleration represents a leap of twenty-two places and an increase in download speed of more than 50 megabits per second, an increase of about twenty-six percent.
La capitale politique enregistre égaleme: The political capital also records a positive dynamic. Algiers progresses by four places to settle at the fifty-ninth global position, displaying an average mobile download speed of 157.34 megabits per second. According to the ministerial department, these results reflect the concrete impact of telecommunication network modernization projects deployed across the entire territory, a dynamic that is progressively extending to other wilayas.
Extension des usages numériques et de la: Extension of digital uses and connectivity
En parallèle des performances techniques: In parallel with technical performance, Internet use continues its expansion among citizens. According to DataReportal's Digital 2026 report, Algeria had thirty-seven million eight hundred thousand internet users at the end of 2025, representing nearly four out of ten inhabitants connected, or exactly 79.5 percent of the population. The country thus integrated one million seven hundred thousand new internet users within the space of a year. Nevertheless, approximately nine million seven hundred thousand people did not have internet access at the same deadline.
Le segment mobile demeure le canal princ: The mobile segment remains the main channel for network access, with the country recording fifty-five million six cent thousand cellular mobile connections, a volume higher than the total population due to multi-SIM ownership. Regarding social networks, twenty-seven million five hundred thousand active identities were recorded in October 2025, or 57.7 percent of the population, with an increase of two million six cent thousand users in twelve months. Facebook leads with a potential advertising audience of twenty-seven million five hundred thousand people, followed by YouTube with twenty-five million four hundred thousand and Instagram with thirteen million five cent thousand.
Enfin, l'enquête Africascope Maghreb 202: Finally, Kantar's Africascope Maghreb 2025 survey indicates that the internet reaches a daily coverage of ninety percent in the country, with individuals dedicating an average of two hours and fifty-one minutes per day to these uses in the Maghreb.
